name: shuffle-hero

frames.best_why: Frame 1 shows the hero settled with all sixteen grid photos in place and the full copy.

tagline: A hero with copy beside a photo grid that reshuffles itself every few seconds.
summary: A split hero: a small orange eyebrow, a large headline, a short paragraph and a call-to-action button on the left, with a 4x4 grid of photos on the right that springs into a new random order every three seconds.
appearance: On black, a left column carries an orange uppercase eyebrow, a large white two-line headline, a grey paragraph and an orange button. To its right a 4x4 grid of closely spaced square photos shows sports and studio activities, filling roughly half the width.
behaviour: Every three seconds the sixteen photos swap places; each tile glides to its new cell with a spring, so briefly the grid opens gaps and tiles overlap before settling. The copy stays put.
demo_content: Fitness copy: 'Let's change it up a bit', a line about sunrise yoga and late-night spin, and 16 sports photos.
search_phrases: landing page headline and image tiles
hero with call to action and gallery
use_when: A landing hero sells a visual product and a static image feels too quiet, but the headline still needs to lead.
avoid_when: The photos reshuffle forever and load from remote URLs, so it costs bandwidth, distracts from reading, and never rests.
customise: There are no props: the eyebrow, headline, paragraph, button text and the sixteen photo URLs are written inside, so all of them need source edits.
weight_why: Sixteen remote photos with spring layout animations every three seconds.

a11y.note: The button is a real button, but the sixteen photos are unlabelled CSS backgrounds and the reshuffle ignores reduced-motion settings.

issues: The grid reshuffles every three seconds with no pause, which can distract from reading the copy.
polish_why: A clean split layout and lively grid; the looping shuffle never pauses and the photos are generic.
